bottom_line: The ratings mostly still hold on their own numbers, but tonight's open is dominated by the Nvidia CEO story, which is the worldview's top named risk. Nasdaq futures are down 0.6-0.8% with Nvidia off 6-7% premarket and no board decision yet, so wait for the first hour and for any announcement before adding.
what_changed: Nvidia fell about 8% after hours and 6-7% premarket on a WSJ report that its board may remove Jensen Huang; Bloomberg says a successor search is under way, with no decision yet. This is the worldview's 'disorderly Nvidia CEO change' risk.
Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.6-0.8% and S&P 500 futures 0.3-0.4% early Thursday, erasing part of Wednesday's CoreWeave-led rally (Semis ETF +4.8%).
Money is rotating inside AI rather than leaving it: AMD rose about 4% and Broadcom about 2% after hours. That supports the power, grid and cooling rotation the worldview is watching.
Analysts told CNBC Nvidia could fall another 20% if Huang goes, which would hit names tied to Nvidia's financing first (CoreWeave, Dell).
